The anonymous public NED TAP service documents programmatic cone searches of the NED Object Directory and requests NED acknowledgment. CTAS retains bounded source-native rows and provenance only. NED states that high-volume automated access is best-effort, so this adapter is single-threaded, starts at most one request per second, and never queries proprietary or user-account holdings.

NOIRLab's provider-owned API authentication notebook states that anyone may retrieve public files while proprietary-file retrieval requires authorization. This adapter sends no credential and retains a product only after an exact file-metadata lookup supplies a nonblank release_date no later than the query time. Anonymous metadata about unreleased files is counted only for exclusion and is never stored. Product bytes are not downloaded.

Rubin alert packets are world-public with no proprietary period, and Fink documents its LSST Science Portal and REST API as real-time, public services requiring no login. Coordinate and first-detection proximity are not proof of source identity.

SIMBAD documents free access without registration under the ODbL license. This adapter uses the anonymous official TAP service for one bounded coordinate query, retains provider attribution and source bibcodes, and does not treat a nearby literature object as the transient, its host, or a new detection.

evidence_timeline.summary: Core collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are invoked as major dust producers in the early Universe, yet the amount of dust they form, the timescale over which it grows, and the physical conditions that regulate the yield remain uncertain. We present a detailed JWST/MIRI mid-infrared (MIR) imaging census of 11 nearby Type IIP CCSNe spanning $\sim$1-7 yr after explosion, investigating dust emission across the different phases of their evolution. The spectral energy distributions show a coherent evolution from hot ($\sim$1500 K), 5-8 $μ$m emission at $\sim$400 d to prominent 10 and 18 $μ$m emission features at later epochs ($\sim$600-2500 d). The cool dust temperatures range from $\sim120$ to $250$ K and dust masses from $\sim10^{-4}$ to $10^{-2} M_{\odot}$. The current sample shows no statistically significant correlation between measured dust mass and peak luminosity, plateau duration, or explosion energy. SNe with early high ionization features, indicative of confined CSM, are often among the dust-rich objects in the sample. The measured 1-7 yr dust yields are insufficient to account for dust in typical $z > 6$ galaxies, but support a role for CCSNe as producers of seed dust for subsequent grain growth.
evidence_timeline.title: A JWST/MIRI Study of Dust in a Sample of Normal Type IIP Core Collapse Supernovae

evidence_timeline.summary: We present optical-ultraviolet photometry and optical spectra for the type II supernova (SN) 2022acko. The spectroscopic observations span phases from <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0001" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>1.5 to <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0002" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>60 d after the explosion, while the light curve was observed up to <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0003" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>300 d. The V-band peak is <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0004" notation="LaTeX">$-15.5 \pm 0.3$</tex-math></inline-formula> mag, suggesting that SN 2022acko is a low-luminosity SN II (LLSN). The overall observed properties of SN 2022acko are consistent with those produced by a lower mass progenitor (<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0005" notation="LaTeX">$\rm M_{ZAMS} \sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>9-10 M<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0006" notation="LaTeX">$_{\odot }$</tex-math></inline-formula>). The spectra at <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0007" notation="LaTeX">$t=1.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d and <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0008" notation="LaTeX">$t=2.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d exhibit a broad emission feature peaking near 4600 Å (the 'ledge' feature), which we interpret as blueshifted He II 4686 Å lines arising from the ionized ejecta. Moreover, a possible flash-ionized (FI) emission line of H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0009" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> (FWHM <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0010" notation="LaTeX">$\sim 1100\ \rm km \ s^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) was superposed on the broad emission component of H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0011" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> P-Cgyni profile in the <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0012" notation="LaTeX">$t=1.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d spectrum. Assuming an ejecta velocity of <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0013" notation="LaTeX">$\rm 12000\ km\ s^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, the rapid disappearance of this narrow H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0014" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> emission line within 2 d suggests highly confined circumstellar material (CSM) within <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0015" notation="LaTeX">$\sim \rm 2\times 10^{14}\, cm$</tex-math></inline-formula>. Assuming a spherically symmetric CSM, the mass loss rate within this radius is estimated to be <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0016" notation="LaTeX">$\rm \sim 5 \times 10^{-4} {\rm M}_{\odot } \ yr^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula> based on our hybrid light curve model. The early 'ledge' feature observed in SN 2022acko have also been observed in other SNe II, suggesting that early-phase circumstellar interaction is more common than previously thought.
evidence_timeline.title: SN 2022acko: a low-luminosity SNe IIP with signs of early circumstellar interaction

publication_revisions.abstract: Core collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are invoked as major dust producers in the early Universe, yet the amount of dust they form, the timescale over which it grows, and the physical conditions that regulate the yield remain uncertain. We present a detailed JWST/MIRI mid-infrared (MIR) imaging census of 11 nearby Type IIP CCSNe spanning $\sim$1-7 yr after explosion, investigating dust emission across the different phases of their evolution. The spectral energy distributions show a coherent evolution from hot ($\sim$1500 K), 5-8 $μ$m emission at $\sim$400 d to prominent 10 and 18 $μ$m emission features at later epochs ($\sim$600-2500 d). The cool dust temperatures range from $\sim120$ to $250$ K and dust masses from $\sim10^{-4}$ to $10^{-2} M_{\odot}$. The current sample shows no statistically significant correlation between measured dust mass and peak luminosity, plateau duration, or explosion energy. SNe with early high ionization features, indicative of confined CSM, are often among the dust-rich objects in the sample. The measured 1-7 yr dust yields are insufficient to account for dust in typical $z > 6$ galaxies, but support a role for CCSNe as producers of seed dust for subsequent grain growth.

publication_revisions.abstract: We present optical-ultraviolet photometry and optical spectra for the type II supernova (SN) 2022acko. The spectroscopic observations span phases from <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0001" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>1.5 to <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0002" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>60 d after the explosion, while the light curve was observed up to <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0003" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>300 d. The V-band peak is <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0004" notation="LaTeX">$-15.5 \pm 0.3$</tex-math></inline-formula> mag, suggesting that SN 2022acko is a low-luminosity SN II (LLSN). The overall observed properties of SN 2022acko are consistent with those produced by a lower mass progenitor (<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0005" notation="LaTeX">$\rm M_{ZAMS} \sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>9-10 M<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0006" notation="LaTeX">$_{\odot }$</tex-math></inline-formula>). The spectra at <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0007" notation="LaTeX">$t=1.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d and <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0008" notation="LaTeX">$t=2.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d exhibit a broad emission feature peaking near 4600 Å (the 'ledge' feature), which we interpret as blueshifted He II 4686 Å lines arising from the ionized ejecta. Moreover, a possible flash-ionized (FI) emission line of H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0009" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> (FWHM <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0010" notation="LaTeX">$\sim 1100\ \rm km \ s^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) was superposed on the broad emission component of H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0011" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> P-Cgyni profile in the <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0012" notation="LaTeX">$t=1.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d spectrum. Assuming an ejecta velocity of <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0013" notation="LaTeX">$\rm 12000\ km\ s^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, the rapid disappearance of this narrow H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0014" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> emission line within 2 d suggests highly confined circumstellar material (CSM) within <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0015" notation="LaTeX">$\sim \rm 2\times 10^{14}\, cm$</tex-math></inline-formula>. Assuming a spherically symmetric CSM, the mass loss rate within this radius is estimated to be <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0016" notation="LaTeX">$\rm \sim 5 \times 10^{-4} {\rm M}_{\odot } \ yr^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula> based on our hybrid light curve model. The early 'ledge' feature observed in SN 2022acko have also been observed in other SNe II, suggesting that early-phase circumstellar interaction is more common than previously thought.

publications.abstract: We present optical-ultraviolet photometry and optical spectra for the type II supernova (SN) 2022acko. The spectroscopic observations span phases from <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0001" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>1.5 to <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0002" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>60 d after the explosion, while the light curve was observed up to <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0003" notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>300 d. The V-band peak is <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0004" notation="LaTeX">$-15.5 \pm 0.3$</tex-math></inline-formula> mag, suggesting that SN 2022acko is a low-luminosity SN II (LLSN). The overall observed properties of SN 2022acko are consistent with those produced by a lower mass progenitor (<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0005" notation="LaTeX">$\rm M_{ZAMS} \sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>9-10 M<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0006" notation="LaTeX">$_{\odot }$</tex-math></inline-formula>). The spectra at <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0007" notation="LaTeX">$t=1.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d and <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0008" notation="LaTeX">$t=2.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d exhibit a broad emission feature peaking near 4600 Å (the 'ledge' feature), which we interpret as blueshifted He II 4686 Å lines arising from the ionized ejecta. Moreover, a possible flash-ionized (FI) emission line of H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0009" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> (FWHM <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0010" notation="LaTeX">$\sim 1100\ \rm km \ s^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) was superposed on the broad emission component of H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0011" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> P-Cgyni profile in the <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0012" notation="LaTeX">$t=1.5$</tex-math></inline-formula> d spectrum. Assuming an ejecta velocity of <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0013" notation="LaTeX">$\rm 12000\ km\ s^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, the rapid disappearance of this narrow H<inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0014" notation="LaTeX">$\alpha$</tex-math></inline-formula> emission line within 2 d suggests highly confined circumstellar material (CSM) within <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0015" notation="LaTeX">$\sim \rm 2\times 10^{14}\, cm$</tex-math></inline-formula>. Assuming a spherically symmetric CSM, the mass loss rate within this radius is estimated to be <inline-formula><tex-math id="TM0016" notation="LaTeX">$\rm \sim 5 \times 10^{-4} {\rm M}_{\odot } \ yr^{-1}$</tex-math></inline-formula> based on our hybrid light curve model. The early 'ledge' feature observed in SN 2022acko have also been observed in other SNe II, suggesting that early-phase circumstellar interaction is more common than previously thought.
